feed.title: Vidhana — Sri Lankan IRD tax and VAT gazettes — vat
feed.subtitle: What changed in the Sri Lankan Inland Revenue gazettes, and what the rule is now. Derived from https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/sitepages/gazette.aspx?menuid=1602

entry.title: 2500/106 [vat] amends 2481/22 and changes when it takes effect
entry.content:
As amended by Gazette 2500/106, the prescribed format and specifications for tax invoices issued by every registered person under the VAT Act apply from 1 October 2026, instead of 1 July 2026. All other requirements in Gazette 2481/22 remain unchanged.
Amends 2481/22 — The format and specification of the Tax Invoice to be issued by every registered person, effective from July 01, 2026, in respect of the Value Added Tax,.
This changes when 2481/22 takes effect. Check the date before acting on 2481/22 itself.
Effective from 2026-08-06.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2026_2500_106_E.pdf

entry.title: 2481/22 [vat] rescinds 2463/05
entry.content:
This notice requires every VAT-registered business to issue tax invoices using the specified format, including supplier and purchaser details, TINs, invoice numbering, supply details, VAT amounts and payment information. As amended by Gazette 2500/106, these requirements apply from October 1, 2026, rather than July 1, 2026; the earlier optional format under Gazette 2463/05 is rescinded from that amended effective date.
Rescinds 2463/05 — The format and specification of the Tax Invoice to be issued by every registered person, effective from January 01, 2026, in respect of the Value Added Tax..
The current document in this rule is now 2500/106 (2026-08-06).
Effective from 2026-10-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2026_2481-22_E.pdf

entry.title: 2463/05 [vat] new: The format and specification of the Tax Invoice to be issued by every registered person, effective from January 01, 2026, in respect of the Value Added Tax.
entry.content:
This gazette specified the tax-invoice format that every VAT-registered person was to use from 1 January 2026, including supplier and purchaser details, invoice numbering, supply information, VAT amounts, payment method, and record retention. As amended by Gazette 2481/22, these specifications were optional until 30 June 2026 and were rescinded from 1 July 2026; a replacement tax-invoice format applies from that date.
The current document in this rule is now 2500/106 (2026-08-06).
Effective from 2026-01-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2025_2463-05_E.pdf

entry.title: 2456/02 [vat] rescinds 1986/09
entry.content:
From 1 October 2025, VAT refunds for eligible exporters, project suppliers and approved projects will be processed under a new risk-based scheme replacing the former SVAT refund arrangements. Low- and medium-risk claims may be refunded without prior verification, while high-risk claims require verification first. Eligible businesses must keep their RAMIS details, bank information, schedules and supporting records accurate and provide information for checks; the gazette also sets October and November 2025 deadlines for closing outstanding SVAT transactions.
Rescinds 1986/09 — Specified the Guidelines to operate Simplified Value Added Tax Scheme that effective from 01.01.2016.
Effective from 2025-10-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2025_2456-02_E.pdf

entry.title: 2443/30 [vat] new: Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002, Procedure for Collecting and Paying Value Added Tax on the Supply of Services by a Non- resident Person through an Electronic Platform in Sri Lanka.
entry.content:
From 1 October 2025, VAT will apply to services supplied in Sri Lanka by non-resident persons through electronic platforms, including cloud services, streaming, online marketplaces, digital advertising and similar services. Non-resident suppliers must register when the stated turnover thresholds are exceeded, charge VAT at the applicable rate (currently 18%), remit it by the 20th of the following month, file quarterly returns and keep records. Consumers may see VAT charged on these services, while platform operators must exclude the value of goods or services supplied directly by the original supplier when calculating their own taxable service value.
Effective from 2025-10-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses; consumers (indirectly, through prices).
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2025_2443-30_E.pdf

entry.title: 2363/22 [vat] rescinds 2295/08 and amends 2282/26
entry.content:
From 1 January 2024, the VAT rate is 18% on imports and supplies of goods and on supplies of services, except for goods covered by paragraph 1(b)(a) of the earlier order. This amends Gazette 2282/26 and rescinds Gazette 2295/08 from the same date, so VAT-registered businesses must apply the revised rate to affected transactions.
Amends 2282/26 — Order under Section 2A of Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002.
Rescinds 2295/08 — Order under Section 2A of Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002.
Effective from 2024-01-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2023_2363-22_E.pdf

entry.title: 2316/13 [vat] rescinds 1868/10
entry.content:
From 1 October 2022, this order sets out how VAT on the supply of financial services must be calculated, including the treatment of profits, employee remuneration, economic depreciation, VAT and SSCL. Businesses must separately identify non-financial services where they keep certified separate accounts, or apportion value addition based on turnover, and submit specified accounts and schedules with the annual return. It rescinds Gazette Extraordinary No. 1868/10 with effect from the same date.
Rescinds 1868/10 — Order to specify matters relating to and the manner in which Tax is calculated in respect of VAT on Financial Services with effect from 01.01.2014.
Effective from 2022-10-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2023_2316-13_E.pdf

entry.title: 2300/25 [vat] amends 2282/26
entry.content:
From 7 October 2022, imports and domestic supplies of sanitary towels (pads) and tampons under H.S. Code 9619.00.10 are subject to VAT at 0%. The order also continues the VAT rates for specified imported goods listed in the schedule to Gazette Notification No. 2095/20.
Amends 2282/26 — Order under Section 2A of Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002.
The current document in this rule is now 2363/22 (2023-12-19).
Effective from 2022-10-07.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses; consumers (indirectly, through prices).
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2300-25_E.pdf

entry.title: 2295/08 [vat] amends 2282/26
entry.content:
This order set VAT on imports and supplies covered by subparagraph (b) at 15% from 1 September 2022. As amended by 2300/25 from 7 October 2022, subparagraph (a) also includes a 0% rate for imported or supplied sanitary towels (pads) and tampons; however, Gazette 2363/22 rescinded this order and replaced the subparagraph (b) rate with 18% from 1 January 2024.
Amends 2282/26 — Order under Section 2A of Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002.
The current document in this rule is now 2363/22 (2023-12-19).
Effective from 2022-09-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses; consumers (indirectly, through prices).
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2295-08_E.pdf

entry.title: 2282/26 [vat] amends 2151/52
entry.content:
This Order replaced the earlier VAT order and set VAT at 12% from 1 June 2022 for imports and supplies not covered by the specified imported-goods schedule. As amended by Gazette 2300/25, sanitary towels (pads) and tampons were made zero-rated from 7 October 2022; as amended by Gazette 2363/22, the general rate became 18% from 1 January 2024, and the 15% rate introduced by Gazette 2295/08 was rescinded.
Amends 2151/52 — Order under Value Added Tax Act, (Hotel & Financial Services, Import or Supply of Goods) w.e.f. 01.12.2019.
The current document in this rule is now 2363/22 (2023-12-19).
Effective from 2022-06-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2022_2282-26_E.pdf

entry.title: 2234/07 [vat] new: Information technology and enabled services prescribe for the purpose of item (Liv) of paragraph (b) of PART II of the First Schedule of the Value Added Tax Act, No. 14 of 2002 as amended by the Value Added Tax (Amendment) Act, No. 9 of 2021
entry.content:
This Order, effective from 1 April 2021, identifies information technology and enabled services that qualify for the treatment under item (Liv) of the VAT Act’s First Schedule. Providers must meet conditions including a 70% local technical employee threshold for software-related services, at least 50% local value addition for most other listed services, and an exclusion for businesses created by splitting up an existing business. The underlying VAT treatment under item (Liv) is not reproduced in this Order.
Effective from 2021-04-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2021_2234-07_E.pdf

entry.title: 2152/60 [vat] amends 2151/52
entry.content:
As amended by Gazette 2152/60, the 0% VAT rule in paragraph 1(a) of Gazette 2151/52 uses a specified earlier taxable period to calculate total inputs. It also defines locally sourced inputs as spending on locally produced agricultural, horticultural, fishing, animal husbandry or dairy products, and locally manufactured goods with at least 10% local value addition.
Amends 2151/52 — Order under Value Added Tax Act, (Hotel & Financial Services, Import or Supply of Goods) w.e.f. 01.12.2019.
The current document in this rule is now 2363/22 (2023-12-19).
Effective from 2019-12-06.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2152-60_E.pdf

entry.title: 2151/52 [vat] new: Order under Value Added Tax Act, (Hotel & Financial Services, Import or Supply of Goods) w.e.f. 01.12.2019
entry.content:
From 1 December 2019, VAT was set at 0% for qualifying services supplied by Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority-registered hotels, guest houses, restaurants and similar businesses where at least 60% of inputs came from local sources; financial services were taxed at 15%, specified imports at their listed rates, and most other imports, goods and services at 8%. The local-input definitions were added by Gazette 2152/60. This position was later rescinded and replaced by Gazette 2282/26 from 1 June 2022, which set the general rate for the covered imports, goods and services at 12%.
The current document in this rule is now 2363/22 (2023-12-19).
Effective from 2019-12-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2151-52_E.pdf

entry.title: 2147/59 [vat] new: Order under Value Added Tax Act, to be Charged on Condominium Housing Units
entry.content:
From 1 November 2019, VAT is charged at 6% on services involving the supply of residential accommodation by selling a condominium housing unit. This affects businesses that make these supplies and may indirectly affect consumers through the price charged.
Effective from 2019-11-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses; consumers (indirectly, through prices).
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2147-59_E.pdf

entry.title: 2125/69 [vat] amends 2124/03
entry.content:
As amended by this Gazette, VAT is charged at 7% on services supplied by Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority-registered hotels, guest houses, restaurants and similar businesses, and on inbound-tour services supplied by registered travel agents. This rate applies from 1 June 2019 to 31 March 2020 and replaces the order published as Gazette 2124/03 from 1 June 2019.
Amends 2124/03 — Value Added Tax Charged on Supply of Services by a Hotel, Travel Agent etc..
Effective from 2019-06-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2125-69_E.pdf

entry.title: 2124/03 [vat] new: Value Added Tax Charged on Supply of Services by a Hotel, Travel Agent etc.
entry.content:
This order imposed 5% VAT on specified services supplied by Tourism Development Authority-registered hotels, guest houses, restaurants and similar businesses, and on inbound tours supplied by registered travel agents, starting 21 May 2019. As amended by Gazette 2125/69, the 5% order was repealed from 1 June 2019 and replaced with a 7% rate for these services until 31 March 2020.
The current document in this rule is now 2125/69 (2019-06-01).
Effective from 2019-05-21.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2019_2124-03_E.pdf

entry.title: 2095/20 [vat] new: Order to declare that the Value Added Tax shall be charged on the importation of Woven Fabrics
entry.content:
VAT is set at 0% on the importation of the listed woven, knitted and related textile fabrics under the specified H.S. codes. This Order rescinds the earlier Order published as Gazette No. 2089/13 dated 17 September 2018, so importers should use this schedule for the covered goods.
Effective from 2018-11-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2095-20_E.pdf

entry.title: 2095/19 [vat] new: Order declare that the Value Added Tax shall be Charged on Wood Sawn or Chipped, Plywood etc.
entry.content:
VAT is charged at 5% on the supply or import of wood products under HS headings 4407 and 4408. This covers wood sawn, chipped, sliced or peeled to a thickness exceeding 6 mm, and specified veneering or plywood-related sheets over 6 mm thick.
Effective from 2018-11-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2095-19_E.pdf

entry.title: 2089/13 [vat] new: Notify under value added tax act to charge on importation of woven Fabrics of silk, carded wool etc.
entry.content:
This Order imposes VAT at 5% on the importation of the listed textile and fabric products, identified by their H.S. codes. It covers a wide range of silk, wool, cotton, flax, synthetic and artificial-fibre fabrics, knitted fabrics, lace, coated fabrics and related textile products.
Effective from 2018-09-17.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2089-13_E.pdf

entry.title: 2088/25 [vat] new: Notify the Operation of Tourist Value Added Tax Refund Scheme (TVRS)
entry.content:
This Gazette sets out the Tourist Value Added Tax Refund Scheme (TVRS). Tourists may claim a refund of 80% of the VAT-exclusive value of eligible goods taken out of Sri Lanka, provided the purchases total at least Rs. 50,000 excluding VAT, are covered by no more than three invoices per day, and are made from an Authorized Retailer. Bottled water, aerated water, cooked meals, and goods that have been fully or partly consumed are excluded.
Effective from 2018-09-11.
Affects: consumers (indirectly, through prices); VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2088-25_E.pdf

entry.title: 2088/02 [vat] new: Notify the operational date on section 58A of Value Added Tax Act
entry.content:
Section 58A of the Value Added Tax Act comes into operation on 11 September 2018. This gazette only sets the commencement date; it does not explain the requirements contained in section 58A.
Effective from 2018-09-10.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2088-02_E.pdf

entry.title: 2078/06 [vat] new: Notify the Regulations for healthcare services for the purpose of Value Added Tax, w.e.f. 02.07.2018
entry.content:
From 2 July 2018, the cost of healthcare services other than hospital room charges is excluded when calculating the value of healthcare supplies for VAT. This replaces and rescinds the earlier healthcare-services order published in Gazette No. 1991/17 dated 1 November 2016.
Effective from 2018-07-02.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2018_2078-06_E.pdf

entry.title: 2042/21 [vat] new: Record Keeping Regulations No. 1 of 2017 under the Value Added Tax Act
entry.content:
These regulations replace the 1998 record-keeping rules and require every VAT-registered business to keep detailed, up-to-date records of taxable, exempt, excluded and suspended supplies, imports, purchases, adjustments and input/output tax. Businesses must maintain specified VAT control accounts, worksheets and schedules, submit the required schedules with VAT returns where applicable, and preserve records for five years after the relevant taxable period. The regulations also include special record and schedule requirements for RIPs, RISs and certain wholesale and retail businesses.
Effective from 2017-10-26.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
(Summary confidence: medium. The gazette itself is the source of truth.)
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2017_2042-21_E.pdf

entry.title: 2012/02 [vat] new: Notification of specify the records to be maintained and procedure to be adopted by persons who registered for Value Added Tax on wholesale and retail trade effective from May 02, 2016,
entry.content:
From 2 May 2016, VAT-registered wholesalers and retailers may claim deemed input VAT on eligible opening stock and purchases from non-VAT-registered suppliers, subject to the stated limits. They must keep specified stock and purchase records, collect supplier documents, submit the required schedules with VAT returns, enter the amounts in the specified return fields, and submit a reconciliation with the Income Tax Return; the maximum retail price cannot be increased because of the credit.
Effective from 2016-05-02.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2017_2012_02_E.pdf

entry.title: 1991/17 [vat] new: Order to prescribe that the Cost of the any Healthcare Service other than the fees paid to medical practitioners, medical consultation fees etc. be excluded in calculating the value for the purpose of VAT w.e.f. 01.11.2016
entry.content:
From 1 November 2016, the cost of healthcare services listed in the Schedule is excluded when calculating the VAT value of a healthcare service. This exclusion does not cover fees paid to medical practitioners, medical consultation fees, channeling fees, or hospital room charges.
Effective from 2016-11-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/1991_17_E.pdf

entry.title: 1986/09 [vat] rescinds 1910/02
entry.content:
This gazette set the operating rules for the Simplified Value Added Tax (SVAT) Scheme, including which qualifying businesses could register, how suspended VAT invoices and credit vouchers had to be handled, and the forms, records and return deadlines that applied. It replaced the earlier 1910/02 guidelines from 1 January 2016. As amended by 2456/02, the SVAT Scheme was later repealed and this gazette rescinded, with the Risk Based Refund Scheme applying from 1 October 2025.
Rescinds 1910/02 — The operation of Simplified Value Added Tax (SVAT) scheme.
The current document in this rule is now 2456/02 (2025-09-29).
Effective from 2016-01-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2016_1986_09_E.pdf

entry.title: 1910/02 [vat] new: The operation of Simplified Value Added Tax (SVAT) scheme
entry.content:
This Gazette set out the registration, invoicing, credit-voucher, return-filing and record-keeping rules for businesses using the Simplified Value Added Tax (SVAT) scheme, including eligible exporters, project participants and their suppliers. The rules are no longer in force: they were rescinded by Gazette 1986/09 with effect from 1 January 2016 and replaced by new SVAT guidelines.
The current document in this rule is now 2456/02 (2025-09-29).
Effective from 2015-04-16.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2015_1910_02_E.pdf

entry.title: 1868/10 [vat] new: Order to specify matters relating to and the manner in which Tax is calculated in respect of VAT on Financial Services with effect from 01.01.2014
entry.content:
This order set out how VAT on financial services was calculated, including the value-addition formula, economic-depreciation rules, applicable rates, return periods and supporting documents for businesses supplying financial services. It applied from 1 January 2014, but was rescinded and replaced by Gazette 2316/13 with effect from 1 October 2022; therefore, these rules are no longer the operative rules for periods from that date.
The current document in this rule is now 2316/13 (2023-01-24).
Effective from 2011-01-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2014_1868_10_(E).pdf

entry.title: 1606/30 [vat] new: Amendment to Gaz. Ex. No. 1310/10 of 14.10.2003 - VAT
entry.content:
This Gazette replaces the schedule of economic depreciation rates in the 2003 VAT order. From 1 April 2009, the specified rates are 25% for data-processing equipment, accessories and software; 20% for motor vehicles; 12.5% for other machinery, plant, equipment, furniture or fixtures; 10% for intangible assets other than goodwill; and 6⅔% for buildings.
Effective from 2009-04-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2009_1606_30 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1582/35 [vat] new: Value Added Tax - Reduction of 15 to 12 per centum w.e.f. 01.01.2009
entry.content:
The standard VAT rate is reduced from 15% to 12%, effective 1 January 2009. This primarily affects VAT-registered businesses, which must charge and account for VAT at the new rate; consumers may be affected through prices.
Effective from 2009-01-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses; consumers (indirectly, through prices).
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/2009_1582_35 (E).pdf

entry.title: 1530/14 [vat] new: Amendment Act No. 6 of 2005. Tax shall be charged at the rate specified in the corresponding entry
entry.content:
A 5% VAT rate is set for imports of the listed goods, including petrol, certain electric filament or discharge lamps, and arc lamp carbon. Goods marked with an asterisk require prior approval from the National Film Corporation before importation.
Effective from 2008-01-01.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/20081530_14(E).pdf

entry.title: 1500/20 [vat] new: Value Added Tax for Salmon, Green grams etc
entry.content:
This Order sets Value Added Tax at 5% on imports of listed fish products, chickpeas and green grams. VAT-registered businesses importing these goods must apply the 5% rate; the Order does not state a separate effective date.
Effective from 2007-06-06.
Affects: VAT-registered businesses.
Source: https://www.ird.gov.lk/en/publications/Gazette_Documents/20071500_20(E).pdf
